summary: Join our specialized training course on infectious disease prevention in rural communities. Equip yourself with essential knowledge to protect public health.
lede: Infectious disease prevention in rural communities helps community health workers and public health teams reduce transmission at home and in shared spaces. It teaches them to identify transmission routes and local risks, plan practical hygiene and WASH measures, and build community surveillance, referral, and outbreak-preparedness processes.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals working in rural and resource-limited settings who are pivotal in infection risk reduction and community health protection.
audience: Community Health Workers (CHWs) and community health
Public health officers and rural health facility
Local government officers and community development staff
School health coordinators and education officers
WASH officers and hygiene promotion teams
Disaster risk reduction (DRR) and emergency preparedness
modules: Foundations of Infectious Disease Prevention in Rural Contexts
Understanding Transmission Routes and Local Risk Drivers
Prevention in Schools, Markets, and Public Spaces
Preventing Respiratory Infections and Community Spread
Community Engagement and Behavior Change for Prevention
Outbreak Preparedness and Rapid Response Basics
Monitoring Prevention Results and Sustaining Change
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of public health principles and experience working in rural or resource-limited settings. Access to a computer and internet connection is required for online resources.
